claims.text: Pulumi emits placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` when an Output is treated as a plain value (e.g., in a log line, generated file, or resource property).
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when an update conflicts with another in-progress update.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs.
The Pulumi CLI produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, documented at the using-a-diy-backend page anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (without apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message.

In TypeScript, the placeholder string for an Output converted to a string contains text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string via f-string produces text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` is the alternative.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In C#, the placeholder string contains text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes converting an Output to string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text, in TypeScript, Python, and C#.

String-composition helpers: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
An `apply` callback runs asynchronously after the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned in it is undefined when read earlier.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept an output.

In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on an Output evaluates the Output object itself and is generally always true; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because Output<bool> is not a bool.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Using an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, `range(some_output)` raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value out of an Output; awaiting or reading it synchronously fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
Linked docs pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
